title: Nova Scotia HST for Online Stores
description: Nova Scotia HST for online stores: the 14% rate since April 1, 2025, rebated kids' items, diapers and books, catching old rates, and Shopify setup.
h1: Selling online to Nova Scotia: the 14% HST and what it covers
name: Nova Scotia
lead: Nova Scotia cut its HST by one point on April 1, 2025, and it is now the only Atlantic province at 14%. Stores that set their rates by hand before the change, or copy rates from older guides, may still be charging the old figure.

facts.label: Tax on a Nova Scotia order
facts.value: 14% HST: 5% federal GST and 9% provincial part

facts.label: Rate change
facts.value: Down from 15% to 14% as of April 1, 2025, with transition rules

facts.label: What is taxable
facts.value: The same tax base as the federal GST

facts.label: Point-of-sale rebate items
facts.value: Books, children's clothing and footwear, and children's diapers

facts.label: Books for the rebate
facts.value: Printed books and audiobooks of printed books; e-books, magazines and agendas are excluded

facts.label: Children's diapers
facts.value: Cloth and disposable diapers, inserts and liners, rubber pants and training pants

facts.label: Goods shipped from another province
facts.value: Taxed in the province they are shipped to, so at the Nova Scotia rate

facts.label: CRA platform example (page dated 2024-10-16)
facts.value: Still shows 15% HST on a Nova Scotia sale

facts.label: GST/HST small supplier limit
facts.value: $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive quarters

sections.h2: The 14% rate, and why your store may not show it
body: Since April 1, 2025, a taxable order delivered in Nova Scotia carries 14% HST, made up of the 5% federal GST and a provincial part of 9%. Before that date the rate was 15%, the same as the other Atlantic provinces. The CRA published transition rules for orders that straddled the change.

Anywhere a rate was typed in by hand can miss a change like this: manual rate tables, custom checkouts, quote templates, invoice templates and accounting integrations. If any part of your system still says 15% for Nova Scotia, it is out of date.

Older guides can mislead you too. A CRA page on platform sales, last modified on 2024-10-16, still uses 15% in an example for a Nova Scotia buyer. The CRA's rates table and the province both give 14%, which is the rate to use.

sections.h2: One account, no separate provincial registration
body: Nova Scotia's HST is administered by the CRA, and the province says its tax base is the same as the federal GST's. A registered store collects it on its normal GST/HST return. There is no Nova Scotia number to apply for, and no provincial threshold separate from the federal small supplier test.

sections.h2: Items where only the federal part applies
body: Nova Scotia rebates its provincial part at the till on three groups of products. On these, a registered seller credits the provincial part at checkout and the customer pays only the federal part.
list: Books: printed books and audiobooks that are readings of printed books. E-books, newspapers, magazines, catalogues, colouring books and agendas are not included.
Children's clothing and footwear in children's sizes. Costumes and sports equipment are excluded.
Children's diapers, cloth or disposable, including inserts, liners, rubber pants and training pants.

sections.h2: How this differs from the neighbours
body: Diapers are the item that sets Nova Scotia apart from New Brunswick and Newfoundland and Labrador, whose rebate covers books only. A baby store shipping across Atlantic Canada needs product rules that change by province: a pack of cloth diapers is rebated in Halifax but carries the full HST in Moncton or St. John's.

Digital products are not on the rebate list in any form. An e-book, a downloadable sewing pattern or a printable planner sold to a Nova Scotia customer carries the full 14% when you are registered, since downloads are generally taxed in the province of the customer's address.

stepsHeading: Check Nova Scotia HST in Shopify

steps.name: Review the Canada region
steps.text: In the Shopify admin, open Settings, then Taxes and duties, then Canada, and confirm your GST/HST number is listed under the regions you collect in.

steps.name: Look for old manual rates
steps.text: If you set rates or overrides by hand before April 1, 2025, find any Nova Scotia entry that still says 15% and correct it.

steps.name: Add rebate overrides
steps.text: Create tax overrides for books, children's clothing and footwear, and diapers so Nova Scotia orders for those items carry only the federal part.

steps.name: Place a Halifax test order
steps.text: Order one rebated item and one regular item to a Nova Scotia postal code and check both tax amounts.

checklist: Search your store, invoices and integrations for any 15% rate tied to Nova Scotia.
Tag books, children's clothing and footwear, and diapers as rebate items for Nova Scotia.
Keep e-books and other downloads at the full rate.
Make sure diapers are not rebated for New Brunswick or Newfoundland and Labrador orders.
Track worldwide taxable sales against the $30,000 small supplier limit.

faqs.q: Is the Nova Scotia HST 15% or 14%?
faqs.a: 14%, as of April 1, 2025. Some older pages and examples still show 15%.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate Nova Scotia tax number?
faqs.a: No. The HST is administered by the CRA and reported on your GST/HST return.

faqs.q: Are e-books rebated like printed books?
faqs.a: No. The rebate's definition of books excludes e-books.
